variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Netflix streaming architecture is the system that prepares a studio video, decides that a member may watch it, and delivers small video pieces to a player that can adapt as its network changes. It separates the control plane (identity, title availability, manifests, and policy) from the media plane (the high-bandwidth video segments delivered close to viewers).
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Ingest converts a source asset into a publishable playback package”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Validate the source
pairs.detail: Check file integrity, duration, audio and subtitle tracks, rights window, and technical metadata.
pairs.explanation: Check file integrity, duration, audio and subtitle tracks, rights window, and technical metadata. Preserve a stable asset identity so retries do not create competing packages.

pairs.label: Encode a rendition ladder
pairs.detail: Produce multiple bitrate and resolution choices for supported codecs and devices.
pairs.explanation: Produce multiple bitrate and resolution choices for supported codecs and devices. Each rung trades visual fidelity against the bandwidth needed to sustain it.

pairs.label: Package and verify
pairs.detail: Split each rendition into aligned segments and manifests.
pairs.explanation: Split each rendition into aligned segments and manifests. Verify timing alignment, playback continuity, captions, audio selection, and content protection metadata before promotion.

pairs.label: Publish immutable outputs
pairs.detail: Write versioned media objects, expose the approved package to delivery caches, and only then allow the catalog to advertise its availability in a region.
pairs.explanation: Write versioned media objects, expose the approved package to delivery caches, and only then allow the catalog to advertise its availability in a region.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Core invariantPlayback must continue within startup, rebuffering, quality, and origin-protection budgets despite variable networks and failures.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Validate the source: Check file integrity, duration, audio and subtitle tracks, rights window, and technical metadata. Encode a rendition ladder: Produce multiple bitrate and resolution choices for supported codecs and devices. Package and verify: Split each rendition into aligned segments and manifests. Publish immutable outputs: Write versioned media objects, expose the approved package to delivery caches, and only then allow the catalog to advertise its availability in a region.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Keep three records separate”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Source asset

pairs.label: Playback package
pairs.detail: Owns rendition IDs, segment maps, audio and subtitle variants, checksums, and publication status.
pairs.explanation: Owns rendition IDs, segment maps, audio and subtitle variants, checksums, and publication status.

pairs.label: Catalog availability
pairs.detail: Owns whether a profile in a region may discover and start a particular approved package.

variants.prompt: A player has 100,000 concurrent viewers at a 5 Mbps rendition and a 1.2 peak factor. What media bandwidth should the edge plan to serve before considering overhead?
options: 60 Gbps
500 Gbps
600 Gbps
6 Tbps

variants.prompt: During a cache miss storm, which mitigation best protects the origin?

Coalesce equivalent fills, bound retries, and use safe fallback or steering
